notes: Hand-checked research. Stances use the -2..2 'agrees with the statement' scale from issues.json. Every stance carries the short summary shown on the card; sources are listed per candidate.

Jocelyn Benson.blurb: Michigan Secretary of State since 2019; former Wayne State law dean. Running on lowering costs for health care, prescriptions and housing.

taxes: Won't raise taxes on the middle class; proposes home-buyer tax credits and cutting government costs instead.
healthcare: "Healthcare should be a right." Would expand low/no-cost preventive care, medical debt relief, $5,000 caregiver credit.
abortion: Supports legal abortion; backed 2022's Proposal 3 that put reproductive rights in the state constitution.
guns: Backs red flag laws, universal background checks and safe storage; banned open carry at polling places in 2020.
immigration: Opposes federal ICE deployments in Michigan and withholding funds from sanctuary cities.
climate: Supports 100% clean electricity by 2040; tougher penalties for polluters and Great Lakes protections.
labor: "Unions built the middle class." Supports collective bargaining and benefits for striking workers.
voting: Opposes proof-of-citizenship requirements; backs a state Voting Rights Act.
lgbtq: Supported adding sexual orientation and gender identity to civil-rights law.
schools: Opposes draining money from neighborhood public schools; OK with charters held to the same standards.
crime: Launched IDs for newly paroled people; focuses on re-entry and police-community trust.
trump: Campaigns against Trump administration tariffs, the Iran war and federal cuts.

John James.blurb: Two-term U.S. Representative (MI-10, Macomb County), Army helicopter pilot in Iraq, businessman. Running on cutting taxes and government waste.

taxes: Would eliminate Michigan's income tax and reform property taxes.
healthcare: "Not more government, it's less." Voted for Medicaid cuts and against extending ACA subsidies; wants Medicaid work requirements.
abortion: Called himself "100% pro-life" (2018); in 2024 said voters "already decided" with Proposal 3.
guns: "SHALL NOT BE INFRINGED." Sponsored national concealed-carry reciprocity.
immigration: Voted for +$75B ICE funding, 900 miles of border wall, E-Verify; opposes sanctuary cities.
climate: Calls the 100% clean-energy-by-2040 law "insane"; prefers "innovation rather than mandates."
labor: Supports right-to-work; has also joined a nurses' picket line and praised UAW workers.
voting: Wants a constitutional amendment requiring proof of citizenship and voter ID.
lgbtq: Voted to ban gender-affirming care for minors and trans girls in girls' sports.
schools: Would opt Michigan into the federal private-school scholarship tax credit "on day one."
crime: "Lock up violent criminals"; more training, equipment and legal protections for police.
trump: Voted for the 2025 federal tax-and-spending law; says he'll break with Trump when Michigan's interests differ.

sources.title: guides.vote: Michigan Governor 2026
Michigan Public: James distances himself from Trump in debate (Oct 7)

Abdul El-Sayed.blurb: Physician by training and former Detroit and Wayne County health director; has never held elected office. Endorsed by Bernie Sanders.

taxes: Higher top rate on income over $1M and a billionaire wealth tax; against corporate tax breaks.
healthcare: Would pass Medicare for All, abolish medical debt and reverse 2025 Medicaid/ACA cuts.
abortion: Would codify Roe v. Wade into federal law; supports funding Planned Parenthood.
guns: Supports red flag laws and banning "guns meant for a theatre of war."
immigration: Path to citizenship, Dream Act, protect birthright citizenship; supports abolishing ICE and restructuring enforcement.
climate: Path to 100% renewable energy; would shut down the Line 5 pipeline.
labor: Would pass the PRO Act; says right-to-work should be illegal.
voting: Opposes voter ID and the SAVE Act; Election Day holiday, no-reason absentee voting.
lgbtq: "I stand with the LGBTQ+ community"; would guarantee civil rights in health care.
schools: Opposes vouchers moving "public money into private pockets."
crime: Opposes cash bail; backs the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act and violence-prevention programs.
trump: Calls the Iran war "illegal and unjustifiable"; campaigns against the Trump agenda.

sources.title: guides.vote: Michigan U.S. Senate 2026

Mike Rogers.blurb: Former seven-term U.S. Representative (MI-8, 2001–2015), ex-FBI agent and House Intelligence chair. Narrowly lost the 2024 Senate race.

taxes: Backs the 2025 "One Big Beautiful Bill" tax cuts: "There's no tax cut I don't like."
healthcare: Wants free-market health plans; voted to repeal the ACA but called defense-for-health-care cuts "a bridge too far."
abortion: "I'm a pro-life guy"; supported overturning Roe but opposes a national ban and says states decide.
guns: "Banning guns isn't going to do it"; supports background checks and enforcing existing laws.
immigration: Finish the border wall, restore Remain in Mexico, oppose sanctuary cities; prioritizes deporting criminals over mass deportation.
climate: Says EV and renewable mandates are "destroying Michigan's auto industry."
labor: Backed the 2023 UAW strike; past votes to limit prevailing-wage rules and the NLRB.
voting: Supports voter ID and would pass the SAVE Act.
lgbtq: Accepts same-sex marriage as law; opposes trans athletes in women's sports; against firing people for being LGBTQ.
schools: Wants Michigan to join the federal private-school scholarship tax credit.
crime: "Back the blue all the way"; urged sending the National Guard to Detroit.
trump: Advised Trump's 2016 transition; supports giving the president authority to continue the Iran war.

proposals.title: Proposal 1: Constitutional convention
proposals.question: Should Michigan hold a convention of elected delegates in 2027 to rewrite the state constitution?
proposals.yes: Starts a rewrite of the whole constitution. Voters would still have to approve the final document. Some Republican legislative leaders have voiced support.
proposals.no: Keeps the constitution as written. Opposed by a coalition of business, labor and voting-rights groups, and by candidates from both parties including Benson and James.

lean.no: Benson, James, and a bipartisan business/labor coalition

sources.title: Votebeat: Proposal 1 explained

proposals.title: Proposal 2: Money out of politics
proposals.question: Ban campaign contributions from regulated utilities and large government contractors, and expand disclosure rules for political ads, including online.
proposals.yes: Becomes law; it would take a three-quarters vote of the Legislature to change. Backed by Michiganders for Money Out of Politics, funded largely by national progressive groups.
proposals.no: Keeps current rules. Opposed by Protect MI Free Speech, funded by business groups including Consumers Energy's parent, Blue Cross and Comcast.
